# Replication: Weiß and Kim (2025)

This page reproduces **Table 8** of @weiss2025. The table reports simulated rejection
rates at level $\alpha = 0.05$ for DGP 4, an SQMA(1,1) model with
$(\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3) = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)$, for the classical spatial ordinal
pattern (SOP) classification and for the three refined ones.

## Libraries

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| message: false
using StatsOrdinalPatterns, Random, Statistics, Printf, DataFrames, Distributions
```

## Statistics of the paper and their types in the package

The four column groups of Table 8 are the `refinement` argument of [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd):

| Table 8 group | `refinement` |
|:--------------|:-------------|
| Ordinary types | [`OrdinaryType()`](../reference/OrdinaryType.qmd) |
| Rotation types | [`RotationType()`](../reference/RotationType.qmd) |
| Direction types | [`DirectionType()`](../reference/DirectionType.qmd) |
| Diagonal types | [`DiagonalType()`](../reference/DiagonalType.qmd) |

The columns within a group are its `chart_choice`:

| Table 8 column | `chart_choice` | Rejects $H_0$ when | Label below |
|:---------------|:---------------|:-------------------|:------------|
| $\tilde{\tau}$ | [`TauTilde()`](../reference/TauTilde.qmd) | $\lvert\tilde{\tau}\rvert > c$ | `tau_tilde` |
| $\widehat{H}$ | [`Shannon(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.Shannon) | rescaled $\widehat{H} > c$ | `H` |
| $\widehat{H}_{ex}$ | [`ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))`](https://juliadynamics.github.io/ComplexityMeasures.jl/stable/information_measures/#ComplexityMeasures.ShannonExtropy) | rescaled $\widehat{H}_{ex} > c$ | `H_ex` |
| $\widehat{\Delta}$ | [`DistanceToWhiteNoise()`](../reference/DistanceToWhiteNoise.qmd) | $\widehat{\Delta} > c$ | `Delta` |

$\tilde{\tau}$ appears in the ordinary group only; the refined classifications have
asymptotic theory for the entropy type charts. The rescaling of the entropy statistics
and the generalized $\chi^2$ critical value are what [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) applies internally, and
[`crit_val_sop`](../reference/crit_val_sop.qmd) returns the critical value for a given scheme, level and field size.

## Setup

DGP 4 is the [`SQMA11`](../reference/SQMA11.qmd) type of the package: `dgp_params` are the $\beta_j$, `eps_params`
are the exponents $(a, b, c)$ of the three error terms, written "$1^a\,2^b\,3^c$" in the
paper, and `M_rows`, `N_cols` are the dimensions of the field. `m` and `n` in the table
are the dimensions of the SOP matrix, so the field is $(m+1) \times (n+1)$.

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Parameters of Table 8 and one field of DGP 4"
β = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)                                # dependence parameters of Table 8
level = 0.05                                       # nominal significance level
sizes = ((10, 10), (15, 15), (20, 20), (40, 25))   # SOP matrix dimensions (m, n)
reps = 10_000                                      # Monte Carlo replications

models = [
    ("DGP4-1", "1² 2² 3²", (2, 2, 2)),
    ("DGP4-2", "1² 2¹ 3²", (2, 1, 2)),
    ("DGP4-3", "1¹ 2¹ 3²", (1, 1, 2)),
    ("DGP4-4", "1² 2¹ 3¹", (2, 1, 1)),
]

entropies = [("H", Shannon(base=exp(1))), ("H_ex", ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1))), ("Delta", DistanceToWhiteNoise())]

schemes = [
    ("ord", OrdinaryType(), vcat([("tau_tilde", TauTilde())], entropies)),
    ("rot", RotationType(), entropies),
    ("dir", DirectionType(), entropies),
    ("diag", DiagonalType(), entropies),
]

stats = ["$(sn)_$(cn)" for (sn, _, cs) in schemes for (cn, _) in cs]   # 13 columns

# One field of the DGP. `fill_mat_dgp_sop!` is the routine the ARL functions of the
# package use internally; it writes into the caller's buffers and returns a view of the
# field. `mat` receives the field, `mat_ma` the errors, `mat_ao` the additive outliers,
# which DGP 4 does not have.
sqma11(eps, m, n) = SQMA11(β, eps, m + 1, n + 1, Normal(0, 1), nothing)

buffers(dgp) = ntuple(_ -> zeros(dgp.M_rows + 1, dgp.N_cols + 1), 3)

draw_field!(dgp, mat, mat_ao, mat_ma) =
    StatsOrdinalPatterns.fill_mat_dgp_sop!(dgp, dgp.dist, dgp.dist_ao, mat, mat_ao, mat_ma)
```

## A single test

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "One field of DGP 4 and one SOP test"
Random.seed!(1)
dgp = sqma11((2, 2, 2), 10, 10)
Y = collect(draw_field!(dgp, buffers(dgp)...))   # copy out of the buffer
test_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=ShannonExtropy(base=exp(1)), refinement=DiagonalType(), alpha=level)
```

## Running the power study

[`crit_val_sop`](../reference/crit_val_sop.qmd) returns the critical value alone, which depends on the field size, the
level and the classification scheme, not on the data, so it is computed once per row of
the table. [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) additionally computes the $p$ value, which for the entropy charts
means evaluating a generalized $\chi^2$ distribution numerically and which a power study
does not use. Each replication then costs one [`stat_sop`](../reference/stat_sop.qmd) pass per classification scheme,
and the charts of that scheme are read off the resulting $\hat{\mathbf{p}}$ with
[`chart_stat_sop`](../reference/chart_stat_sop.qmd).

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Rejection rates of the 13 tests for one field size"
# two sided for τ̃, upper tail on the rescaled statistic for the entropy charts
rejects(::TauTilde, p̂, crit) = abs(chart_stat_sop(p̂, TauTilde())) > crit
rejects(cc, p̂, crit) =
    StatsOrdinalPatterns.rescale_sop(chart_stat_sop(p̂, cc), length(p̂), cc) > crit

function power(m, n, eps, reps; level=0.05)
    dgp = sqma11(eps, m, n)
    M, N = dgp.M_rows, dgp.N_cols
    crits = [crit_val_sop(M, N, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, refinement=ref, alpha=level)
             for (_, ref, cs) in schemes for (_, cc) in cs]

    tasks = map(Iterators.partition(1:reps, cld(reps, Threads.nthreads()))) do idx
        Threads.@spawn begin
            bufs = buffers(dgp)                     # one set of buffers per task
            hits = zeros(Int, length(crits))
            for _ in idx
                Y = draw_field!(dgp, bufs...)
                k = 0
                for (_, ref, cs) in schemes
                    p̂ = stat_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)), refinement=ref)[2]
                    for (_, cc) in cs
                        k += 1
                        hits[k] += rejects(cc, p̂, crits[k])
                    end
                end
            end
            hits
        end
    end
    return sum(fetch.(tasks)) ./ reps
end
```

The shortcut has to give the same decision as [`test_sop`](../reference/test_sop.qmd) in all 13 columns, not merely a
similar one:

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Check against test_sop"
let dgp = sqma11((1, 1, 2), 20, 20), M = 21, N = 21
    Y = collect(draw_field!(dgp, buffers(dgp)...))
    ok = true
    for (_, ref, cs) in schemes
        p̂ = stat_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=Shannon(base=exp(1)), refinement=ref)[2]
        for (_, cc) in cs
            r = test_sop(Y, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, refinement=ref, alpha=level)
            c = crit_val_sop(M, N, 1, 1; chart_choice=cc, refinement=ref, alpha=level)
            ok &= c ≈ r.asymp_crit && rejects(cc, p̂, c) == r.asymp_reject
        end
    end
    (shortcut_matches_test_sop=ok,)
end
```

::: {.callout-note}
With `reps = 10_000` the page runs in a few seconds and the standard error of a rejection
rate is at most $\sqrt{0.25 / 10^4} = 0.005$.
:::

## Table 8: DGP 4, $(\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3) = (0.8, 0.8, 0.8)$

```{julia}
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Run the study for every model and field size"
res = Dict(
    (name, m, n) => power(m, n, eps, reps; level=level)
    for (name, _, eps) in models for (m, n) in sizes
)
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
tab = DataFrame(
    model=[name for (name, _, _) in models for _ in sizes],
    label=[lab for (_, lab, _) in models for _ in sizes],
    m=[m for _ in models for (m, _) in sizes],
    n=[n for _ in models for (_, n) in sizes],
)
for (j, nm) in enumerate(stats)
    tab[!, nm] = [round(res[(name, m, n)][j], digits=3) for (name, _, _) in models for (m, n) in sizes]
end

function group_table(sn, cs)
    df = DataFrame(model=tab.model, label=tab.label, m=tab.m, n=tab.n)
    for (cn, _) in cs
        df[!, cn] = tab[!, "$(sn)_$(cn)"]
    end
    df
end
```

### Ordinary types

```{julia}
#| echo: false
group_table("ord", schemes[1][3])
```

### Rotation types

```{julia}
#| echo: false
group_table("rot", entropies)
```

### Direction types

```{julia}
#| echo: false
group_table("dir", entropies)
```

### Diagonal types

```{julia}
#| echo: false
group_table("diag", entropies)
```

The paper prints the largest power value of each row in bold:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
maxima = [maximum(tab[i, s] for s in stats) for i in 1:nrow(tab)]
winners = [[s for s in stats if tab[i, s] == maxima[i]] for i in 1:nrow(tab)]
DataFrame(
    model=tab.model, m=tab.m, n=tab.n,
    max_stat=[length(w) <= 3 ? join(w, ", ") : "$(length(w)) columns tied" for w in winners],
    rate=maxima,
)
```

```{julia}
cmp = DataFrame(model=String[], m=Int[], n=Int[], statistic=String[],
    paper=Float64[], replicated=Float64[], dev=Float64[])
for (name, _, _) in models, (m, n) in sizes, (j, nm) in enumerate(stats)
    r = res[(name, m, n)][j]
    push!(cmp, (name, m, n, nm, published[(name, m, n)][j], round(r, digits=3),
        round(r - published[(name, m, n)][j], digits=3)))
end
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
@printf("entries compared:           %d\n", nrow(cmp))
@printf("largest absolute deviation: %.3f\n", maximum(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("mean absolute deviation:    %.3f\n", mean(abs, cmp.dev))
@printf("Monte Carlo standard error: at most %.3f\n", sqrt(0.25 / reps))
```

The five largest deviations:

```{julia}
#| echo: false
first(sort(cmp, :dev, by=abs, rev=true), 5)
```
